newsitem.title: SWEDEN: P&U extends reinvestment scheme to Swedes.
newsitem.headline: P&U extends reinvestment scheme to Swedes.

text.p: U.S.-Swedish drugs group Pharmacia & Upjohn has extended to its Swedish shareholders a reinvestment programme with the lowest minimum brokerage fee on the market, a Swedish newspaper said on Wednesday.

Business daily Finanstidningen said P&U charged a 0.2 percent handling fee for buying or selling its share and had a minimum brokerage fee of 25 crowns. Most banks in Sweden have a minimum fee of nearly 200 crowns.
Shareholders can choose between receiving their dividends in cash or in shares in the company to the same value. There are no fees for reinvestment.
American shareholders in P&U have had the choice of reinvesting their dividends in the company since the 1970's, Finanstidningen quoted Lars Ousback, manager of a P&U unit in Sweden, as saying.

"Nobody is too small to be a shareholder in P&U and we want to look after our smaller shareholders. Therefore, we make it easier for them to gradually increase their stake in P&U through the reinvestment program," Ousback said.
